assertions.preferred_statement: fine-tuning geneformer significantly boosts predictive accuracy for transcription factor regulatory range compared to alternative methods.
tahoe-100m is the largest single-cell dataset to date enabling ai-driven models to learn context-dependent gene functions.

gears significantly outperforms all baseline methods in predicting single-gene perturbation transcriptional responses on both rpe-1 and k562 datasets with m.s.e. improvement of 30-50% and pearson correlation more than double that of baselines.
gears outperforms baseline methods in predicting two-gene perturbation outcomes across all generalization classes with over 30% improvement in m.s.e. and 50% greater enrichment for top de genes.
cellot outperforms current methods scgen cae popalign at predicting single-cell drug responses across both 4i and scrna-seq data modalities.
geneformer encodes network hierarchy in its attention weights in a completely self-supervised manner during pretraining.

gears significantly outperforms cpa in predicting non-additive combinatorial perturbation effects across multiple genetic interaction subtypes with correlation coefficients 0.4 vs 0.0 and precision 10 improvements >40% for four of five subtypes.
cell line identity and cell cycle phase are the major factors driving stratification in the tahoe-100m transcriptomic data.
cellot captures cell-to-cell variability and heterogeneous subpopulation structures better than autoencoder-based methods.
cpa can be applied to combinatorial genetic perturbations and impute missing combinations.
cellot can generalize to unseen patients in lupus ifn-β response prediction outperforming baselines in both i.i.d. and o.o.s. settings.
generalization of cellot to unseen patients requires similar samples in the unperturbed setting and similar perturbation responses in the training set.
crispr-mediated knockout of gsn and pln in ttn+/- cardiac microtissues significantly improves contractile stress validating them as therapeutic targets for dilated cardiomyopathy.
in silico deletion of gata4 or tbx5 in fetal cardiomyocytes is more deleterious to their direct targets compared to indirect targets or housekeeping genes.
cpa can predict out-of-distribution drug combinations and outperforms baseline models.
dabrafenib elicits a stronger transcriptomic response in braf-mutated cell lines compared to kras-mutated or wild-type lines.
crispr-mediated knockout of tead4 in ipsc-derived cardiac microtissues causes a significant reduction in contractile stress.
chemcpa outperforms cpa for combinatorial drug prediction when using chemical priors.
rmc-6236 shows a greater transcriptomic effect in kras-mutated cell lines than in wild-type lines.
fine-tuning geneformer significantly boosts predictive accuracy for chromatin dynamics tasks compared to alternative methods.
the mosaic platform reduces batch effects and enables parallel profiling of thousands of conditions at single-cell resolution.
cpa significantly outperforms scgen in variance and whole distribution prediction.
cpa imputed 5 329 missing combinations in perturb-seq demonstrating applicability to genetic combinatorial screens.
